name: The Dark Woods
attribution: Dungeon World © Sage LaTorra and Adam Koebel. Source: Sagelt/Dungeon-World.

monsters.name: Assassin Vine
monsters.description: Among the animals there exists a clear division 'tween hunter and hunted. Such a split cuts the world of leaves and flowers in twain, as well. Paths into the deep woods covered in creeping vines, and with a snap, these hungry ropes snap tight, dragging their meaty prey into the underbrush.

monsters.name: Blink Dog
monsters.description: Now you see it, now you don't. Hounds once owned by a sorcerer lord and imbued with a kind of illusory cloak, they escaped into the woods and began to breed with wolves and wild dogs. Spotted by the glittering silver of their coats and their strange, ululating howls, they have a remarkable talent for being not quite where they appear to be.
moves: Give the appearance of being somewhere they're not

monsters.name: Centaur
monsters.description: It will be a gathering of clans unseen in this age. Too long have the men cut the ancient trees for their ships. It will be a cleansing fire from the darkest woods. Raise the red banner of war! Today we strike back against these apes and retake what is ours!

monsters.name: Chaos Ooze
special_qualities: Fragments of other planes embedded in it
monsters.description: The barrier between Dungeon World and the elemental planes is not, as you might hope, a wall of stone—it's much more porous. Bits and pieces of the chaos spill out, squirming and squishing around, warping all it touches into some other, strange form. Chaos begets chaos, and it grows.
moves: Cause a change in appearance or substance

monsters.name: Cockatrice
monsters.description: A lizard of a sort, with a beak and gray feathers like a chicken. Found in a nest at the foot of a tree, quick to peck at anyone who tries to steal its eggs—and its victims freeze up all frozen, like a dog left out overnight in winter.
moves: Start a slow transformation to stone

monsters.name: Dryad
monsters.description: More beautiful by far than any man or woman born in the civil realms. To gaze upon one is to fall in love, deep and punishing. Their love is a primal thing, married to the woods—to a great oak that serves as home and mother and sacred place to them. It's a curse to see one; they'll never love you back.

monsters.name: Eagle Lord
monsters.description: Some the size of horses. Bigger, even—the kings and queens of the eagles. The ancient wizards forged a pact with them in the primordial days: men would take the plains and valleys and leave the mountaintops to the eagle lords. Lucky are the elves, for the makers of their treaties yet live.

monsters.name: Elvish Warrior
monsters.description: As with all things they undertake, the elves approach war as an art. A warrior-maiden clad in plate that shone like the winter sky, seeming to glide between the trees the way an angel might, striking out and bathing her blade in blood that steamed in the cold air.

monsters.name: Elvish High Arcanist
monsters.description: True elvish magic isn't like the spells of men. Mannish wizardry is all rotes and formulas; elvish magic requires a fine ear to hear the arcane symphony that sings in the woods and the voice with which to harmonize with what is already resounding. The High Arcanists have become more and less than any elf; the beat of their blood is the throbbing of all magic in this world.
moves: Work the magic that nature demands

monsters.name: Griffin
monsters.description: These creatures have the regal haughtiness of a lion and the arrogant bearing of an eagle, tempered with the unshakeable loyalty of both. To earn the friendship of a griffin is to have an ally all your living days. If you're ever lucky enough to meet one, be respectful and deferential above all else.

monsters.name: Hill Giant
monsters.description: Ever seen an ogre before? Bigger than that. Dumber and meaner, too. Hope you like having cows thrown at you.

monsters.name: Ogre
monsters.description: Somewhere in the not-so-long history of the mannish race there was a divide: one camp built the first city to honor the gods, the others retreated into darkness and grew tall and strong and full of hate. We have forged steel and they match it with their savagery.
monsters.instinct: To return the world to darker days

monsters.name: Razor Boar
monsters.description: The tusks of the razor boar shred metal plate like so much tissue. Voracious, savage and unstoppable, they tower over their mundane kin. A razor boar killed the Drunkard King in a single thrust, so they say.

monsters.name: Satyr
monsters.description: One of only a very few creatures found in the old woods that don't outright want to maim, kill, or eat us. They dwell in glades pierced by the sun, dancing on their funny goat-legs to enchanting music. They smile easily and treat our kind with friendliness, so long as you please them—but very few things hold a grudge like the stubborn satyr.
moves: Pull others into revelry through magic
Play jokes with illusions and tricks

monsters.name: Sprite
monsters.description: I'd classify them elementals, except that 'being annoying' isn't an element.
moves: Play a trick to expose someone's true nature

monsters.name: Treant
monsters.description: Old and tall and thick of bark, walk amidst the tree-lined dark. Strong and slow and forest-born, treants anger quick, we warn: if to woods with axe ye go, know the treants be thy foe.

monsters.name: Werewolf
monsters.description: Cursed, passed on by a bite to make more of their kind—the sorcerer-kings called it 'lycanthropy' in their day. There is no cure. A werewolf transforms to pass unnoticed as beast or man, hunting like both, dreading what they must ask a loved one to do to end it.
monsters.instinct: To shed the appearance of civilization
moves: Transform to pass unnoticed as beast or man

monsters.name: Worg
monsters.description: As horses are to the civil races, so go the worg to the goblins. Mounts, fierce in battle, ridden by only the bravest and most dangerous, are found and bred in the forest primeval to serve the goblins in their wars on men.
